entries.test: Public controlled evaluations of AI systems available at publication and well-motivated humans distinguishing jokes and fiction from factual accounts would test the asserted difference in ability.
entries.note: The claim concerns systems current in April 2025 and makes a categorical assertion about their ability.

entries.test: Public evaluations showing whether contemporary AI systems independently identify and explain errors or contradictions in unfamiliar material would test the assertion that they never critically assess data.
entries.note: In context, critical reflection has a behavioral reading: assessing whether information is reasonable or true.

entries.test: Public controlled evaluations using newly constructed material would test whether contemporary LLMs merely reproduce supplied information or can assess its plausibility and reject unsupported claims.
entries.note: The added plausibility clause is supported by the surrounding contrast with skeptical humans and the explicit denial of critical reflection.
